title: Transactional Reconciler SDK + Webhook Bridge for Optimize Suggestions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We need a safer, observable path for Optimize to publish batching/caching recommendations and have control planes (hosted/dedicated/private) apply them with transactional guarantees. Current automation has occasional double-applies, partial failures during network flaps, and insufficient visibility into what was actually committed versus suggested. This ticket implements (1) a reconciler SDK used by control planes and operators to perform exactly-once suggestion commits and rollbacks, and (2) a webhook bridge + lightweight API endpoints that let Optimize automation push proposals and track acknowledgement states.
goals: 1) Provide an SDK with a single high-level call that performs a transactional apply or rollback with idempotency tokens and durable audit logs. 2) Define a webhook contract that supports retryable deliveries, typed ACK/NACK, and delayed DLQ. 3) Expose an API endpoint for long-running apply operations that returns operation IDs and supports status polling and cancellation. 4) Add observability (per-operation tracing, token-level cost deltas, and metric hooks) and a migration plan for existing consumers.
non_goals: We will not modify model-level recommendations or the Optimize recommendation engine in this ticket. Schema changes to customer config formats are out of scope; adapters will translate where necessary.
acceptance_criteria:
- SDK provides Apply(transactionRequest) -> OperationID and guarantees exactly-once semantic for idempotency tokens.
- Webhook contract published in docs with examples for 3 delivery outcomes (ACK, NACK-retryable, NACK-fatal) and expected idempotency behaviour.
- API endpoints: POST /optimize/v1/proposals (accepts proposals, returns operation id), GET /optimize/v1/operations/{id}, POST /optimize/v1/operations/{id}/cancel implemented and tested.
- End-to-end integration tests covering network retry, partial failure, and DLQ path.
- Canary rollout plan and runbook for rollback in case of systemic failures.
- Dashboard widgets added to Console showing operation latency, success rate, and cost deltas per operation.
technical_design: High level: When Optimize issues a suggestion, it POSTs to /optimize/v1/proposals with a client-generated idempotency_token and proposal payload. The bridge enqueues the proposal into an internal operations table with status PENDING and operation_id (uuid). Consumers (Dedicated / Private reconciler) call SDK.Apply(operation_id, idempotency_token). SDK steps: 1) Acquire advisory lock at operation_id scope (DB row lock or distributed lock) to serialize attempts. 2) Validate proposal against current live config. 3) Begin DB transaction: write commit record with token and 'IN_PROGRESS' state, snapshot affected resources, persist pre-change checksum. 4) Execute apply via existing config apply primitives (exposing a safe commit API to lower layers). 5) On success, persist commit record with 'DONE' and publish event to event bus; release lock. 6) On transient errors, SDK marks operation as RETRYABLE and retries according to backoff; persistent/fatal errors mark as FAILED. Idempotency: Replays with same token consult commit record and behave as no-op if DONE, or resume/rollback if IN_PROGRESS depending on stage. For private deployments where advisory locks may not be available, SDK falls back to optimistic concurrency using config checksums and a compare-and-swap commit step.
webhook_contract:
- Delivery: POST with operation_id, idempotency_token, proposal, metadata.
- Response codes: 200 (ACK-scheduled), 409 (already handled), 5xx (retry), 422 (fatal rejection).
- Headers: X-Optimize-Signature, X-Optimize-Delivery-Attempt, X-Optimize-Idempotency.
- Retries: exponential backoff up to configurable attempts, then DLQ.
- Backpressure: webhooks may include a rate-limit response with Retry-After; Optimize will throttle accordingly.
sdk_surface:
- Apply(ctx, operation_id, idempotency_token, options) -> (operationResult, error)
- Rollback(ctx, operation_id, reason) -> (rollbackResult, error)
- OperationStatus(ctx, operation_id) -> (status, metadata)
- Hooks: OnBeforeCommit, OnAfterCommit, OnFailure for observability integrations.
- Language bindings: Go (primary), TypeScript (control-plane shim), Python (for ad-hoc tools).
observability_metrics:
- optimize.operations.created_total, optimize.operations.succeeded_total, optimize.operations.failed_total, optimize.operations.duration_seconds_bucket, optimize.operations.retries_total, optimize.operations.dlq_total
- tracer tags: operation_id, proposal_type, customer_id, apply_duration_ms
- Console dashboard: per-customer recent operations, avg commit latency, cost delta histogram
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 10% of Optimize proposals target the new webhook bridge; consumers must implement SDK Apply and report status. Phase 2: 50% traffic, enable DLQ processing. Phase 3: global switch with monitoring guardrails. Rollback: ability to cancel operations via API and automated revert scripts generated by SDK that leverage pre-change snapshot. For Dedicated customers, migration will be opt-in with a compatibility shim for older agents.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for SDK idempotency state machine.
- Integration tests simulating concurrent Apply requests with same idempotency_token.
- Chaos tests: network partitions, DB failures, partial apply failures, and replay semantics.
- End-to-end QA with a staging cluster that mimics Dedicated/Private constraints.
- Performance: stress test 500 ops/sec for batching recommendation bursts and ensure median apply latency < 1200ms for small configs.
runbook_high_level:
- If mass failures (>3% of ops) observed: pause webhook deliveries, switch to read-only mode for ops, alert SRE/PM.
- If stuck IN_PROGRESS operations exceed threshold: attempt automated rollback via SDK Rollback(); if rollback fails, escalate to on-call for manual intervention.
- Restore flow for false-positive cost recs: a revert operation is created and executed with pre-snapshot data.
